# Forza Horizon 6 Guide — Horizon Japan

> Unofficial fan strategy guide. Primary source: the English Wikipedia article on Forza Horizon 6. 
> Gameplay detail where Wikipedia is silent is drawn from community guides (Reddit, IGN, GamesRadar, game8, Red Bull, Polygon) and labelled community-sourced. No car names, locations, or stats are invented.

**An unofficial, source-checked guide to the festival in Japan** — Forza Horizon 6 lands in a fictionalised Japan with the biggest map the series has ever built — 636 cars in the live roster today (550+ at launch). This guide covers the car list, Car Pass and DLC packs, barn finds, treasure cars, the Estate, the interactive Japan map, and a beginner path to Horizon Legend — with sources noted for everything.

## Key facts (Wikipedia-confirmed)
- **Setting**: Japan (fictionalised)
- **Released**: May 19, 2026
- **Cars at launch**: 636 in the live roster (550+ at launch, as of Aug 13, 2026)
- **Developer**: Playground Games
- **Publisher**: Xbox Game Studios
- **Platforms**: PC · Xbox Series X|S (PS5 delayed — TBC)
- **Game Pass**: Day one (Ultimate & PC)
- **Garages**: 8 (fast-travel)
- **The Eliminator**: up to 72 players

## Release status (checked August 31, 2026)
- **Released**: May 19, 2026 (Premium early access May 15) — out now.
- **Platforms**: Xbox Series X|S and Windows PC (Steam, Microsoft Store). Xbox Cloud Gaming via Game Pass Ultimate.
- **Game Pass**: Day one on Game Pass Ultimate & PC Game Pass.
- **PlayStation 5**: Delayed — date TBC (not expected in 2026). Wikipedia lists a planned PS5 version; on Aug 27, 2026 Tom Warren (The Verge) said he does not expect it on PS5 in 2026 and IGN reported the same from its own sources. Warren stressed it is delayed, not cancelled. Microsoft and Playground Games have not confirmed a revised date.

## Beginner's guide (path to Horizon Legend)
New to Horizon Japan? Follow this path — distilled from the Reddit no-spoiler guide, RedBull tips, Polygon's 10 tips, and the official First Drive, cross-checked against Wikipedia's confirmed systems.

### 1. Qualify, then Invitational
Run the Horizon Qualifiers, then the Horizon Invitational. Finishing it grants your first (Yellow) Wristband and unlocks the festival, multiplayer, and free cars.

### 2. Pick a starter that matches your style
Silvia K'S for drift, Celica GT-Four for balance, GMC Jimmy for off-road. All three end up in your garage anyway.

### 3. Don't blow credits at the Autoshow
Wheelspins, story events, and the Festival Playlist hand out cars fast. Spend early credits tuning your starter instead.

### 4. Earn Discover Japan stamps
Explore regions, discover landmarks, and photograph them. Stamps feed your Collection Journal and unlock content [WIKI].

### 5. Farm mascots
Mascots sit across the map — drive through them for credits. (Exact count is community-reported; clear them as you explore.)

### 6. Grab Aftermarket Cars
Watch the minimap for green CT car icons. They're secondhand, fully tuned, and cheaper than the Autoshow.

### 7. Use ANNA when you're tired
The AI assistant can drive you to a destination; Cinema Mode hides the UI for screenshot tours.

### 8. Nail Drag Meets
Handbrake + launch control, release on the final light. Jumping the gun lurches you forward.

### 9. Three-star PR stunts
Speed Zones, Danger Signs, and Drift Zones earn Super Wheelspins and Skill Points for Car Mastery trees.

### 10. Turn up difficulty for credits
Higher difficulty + assists off can pay up to +125% credits per race. Only when you can still win.

### 11. Photo everything
Press Up for photo mode. The Horizon Promo challenge gives festival points per car photographed, and the journal wants landmark shots.

### 12. Fast-travel smart
You can teleport to almost anywhere you've already visited — including the middle of a road. Explore first, blink later.

### 13. Unlock the Estate
The Estate is your customisable mountainside property in rural Japan [WIKI] — build and decorate it, and collect daily credit payouts via the My Horizon message center.

### 14. Treasure & Barn loop
9 Treasure Cars hide behind photo clues (no marker until found, no progression needed, no restoration wait). 15 Barn Finds appear as rumours once your Discover Japan stamps unlock them, then need real-time restoration. Both rosters are fully listed on the Cars page.

### Recommended settings
- Enable Proximity Radar (HUD & Gameplay) to see cars behind you.
- Raise camera FOV (Video) for a wider view.
- Build your own music playlist — the 9 in-game stations repeat fast.
- Turn off car damage if you'd rather keep cars pristine.

## Best cars by discipline
Forget hunting for one 'best' car — Horizon is built so different machines win at different things. These are the standout picks for each discipline, pulled from the walkthrough reward cars and what reviewers actually rated.

### Top Speed / Fastest
- **GMA T.50** — Reward for Speed Traps — a raw, lightweight hypercar.
- **Koenigsegg Agera RS** — Granted for discovering Japanese landmarks via Explore Japan.
- **2025 GR GT Prototype** — The cover car; built for straight-line pace.
- **Nissan Nismo GT-R '24** — Top reward from Touge & Street Rivals.

### Drifting
- **Nissan 240 #777** — Drift Club Japan reward — purpose-built slide machine.
- **Mazda RX-8 #99** — Drift Zones reward; rotary balance.
- **Nissan Silvia K'S (starter)** — Rocket-Bunny-style starter that rewards precise throttle.
- **Mazda RX-7 Type R** — Featured in the prologue Touge intro.

### Drag Racing
- **M12S Warthog CST** — Danger Signs reward; brutal launch.
- **Ram 1500 TRX** — First-wristband reward with serious grunt.
- **RJ Anderson #37 Polaris RZR Pro 4** — Prologue truck; strong off-the-line.

### Off-road / Rally
- **Lamborghini Huracán Sterrato** — Dirt Racing max reward.
- **Mini JCW Buggy** — Cross Country reward.
- **#37 Pro 2 Truck** — Cross Country Rivals reward.
- **GMC Jimmy (starter)** — Surprisingly capable in the snowy north.

### Best All-rounder Starter
- **Toyota Celica GT-Four ST205** — Balanced AWD turbo — comfortable on road and light trails while you learn.

### Best Cars FAQ

**Q: Is there one single best car in Forza Horizon 6?**
No. The right car depends on the job — top speed, drift, drag, off-road and all-round driving each favour different builds. Use the picks above as a starting point and tune to taste.

**Q: What is the best all-rounder starter car?**
The Toyota Celica GT-Four ST205: a balanced AWD turbo that is comfortable on road and light trails while you learn the map. The Nissan Silvia K'S is the better pick if you want to learn drifting, and the GMC Jimmy if you'll spend time off-road or in the snow.

**Q: What is the fastest car, and how do I unlock it?**
The GMA T.50 is the top-speed pick and is granted for clearing Speed Traps. The Koenigsegg Agera RS comes from discovering Japanese landmarks via Explore Japan, and the 2025 GR GT Prototype (the cover car) is built for straight-line pace.

**Q: What is the best car for drifting?**
The Nissan 240 #777 (Drift Club Japan reward) and the Mazda RX-8 #99 (Drift Zones reward) are purpose-built slide machines; the Nissan Silvia K'S starter also rewards precise throttle control.

**Q: What is the best car for drag racing?**
The M12S Warthog CST (Danger Signs reward) has a brutal launch, the Ram 1500 TRX is a first-wristband reward with serious grunt, and the RJ Anderson #37 Polaris RZR Pro 4 is strong off the line.

**Q: What is the best off-road / rally car?**
The Lamborghini Huracán Sterrato (Dirt Racing max reward) and the Mini JCW Buggy (Cross Country reward) handle loose surfaces best; the #37 Pro 2 Truck and GMC Jimmy are solid too.

**Q: How many cars are in Forza Horizon 6 at launch?**
636 in the live roster (Aug 13, 2026); 550+ at launch [WIKI]. The lists above are curated, sourced picks — not the full roster.

**Q: What is the best car for farming credits?**
Any of the fast event-reward cars above will do; pair it with higher difficulty and assists off for up to +125% credit payouts, and three-star PR stunts for Super Wheelspins.

## Interactive map — regions of Japan
Forza Horizon 6 is set in a fictionalised Japan with the largest open-world map in the series [WIKI]. The areas below are named in Wikipedia; community guides report the full map spans 10 regions — we list what is encyclopaedically confirmed and clearly mark the rest.

### Tokyo (confirmed)
The largest urban area in any Forza Horizon game — about five times the size of previous city areas [WIKI]. Districts include Shibuya Crossing, Ginko Avenue, and Tokyo Tower, linked by elevated highways. Mix of neon downtown, suburbs, and industrial docks [WIKI].
Highlights: Shibuya Crossing; Ginko Avenue; Tokyo Tower; Elevated highways; Neon downtown · suburbs · industrial docks; ≈5× the size of prior city areas [WIKI].

### Legend Island (confirmed)
A special area unlocked with the Gold Wristband, featuring unique challenges, exclusive events, and a second Horizon Festival [WIKI].
Highlights: Gold Wristband unlock; Unique challenges; Exclusive events; Second Horizon Festival.

### Rural Japan (confirmed)
The countryside, home to the Estate — your customisable mountainside property [WIKI]. Scenic driving and overlooks.
Highlights: The Estate (customisable property); Mountainous scenery; Open-world building.

### Mount Fuji (confirmed)
Japan's iconic peak appears as a backdrop behind Tokyo and the key art — a landmark rather than a drivable district [WIKI].
Highlights: Backdrop landmark; Visible from Tokyo; Key-art centerpiece.

### Hokkaido (community-reported)
Community-reported northern region — snow-covered tundra and ice-road driving. Named by community guides; not officially confirmed by Wikipedia.
Highlights: Community: snow & ice driving; Northernmost area; Contributes to Discover Japan stamps.

### Tohoku (community-reported)
Community-reported northeast region of mountain passes and coastal roads. Not officially named by Wikipedia.
Highlights: Community: mountain passes; Coastal drives; Discover Japan stamps.

### Chubu (community-reported)
Community-reported central-Honshu region — the Japan Alps and long tunnel networks. Not officially named by Wikipedia.
Highlights: Community: Japan Alps; Tunnel networks; Discover Japan stamps.

### Kansai (Osaka) (community-reported)
Community-reported region around the old capital — dense city grid and highway networks. Not officially named by Wikipedia.
Highlights: Community: urban grid; Highway network; Discover Japan stamps.

### Kyushu (community-reported)
Community-reported southwest region of volcanic terrain and winding coastal roads. Not officially named by Wikipedia.
Highlights: Community: volcanic terrain; Coastal winding roads; Discover Japan stamps.

### Okinawa (community-reported)
Community-reported southern island chain — flat island roads and beachfront straights. Not officially named by Wikipedia.
Highlights: Community: island roads; Beachfront straights; Discover Japan stamps.

### Map legend
- PR Speed Traps, Speed Zones, Danger Signs, Drift Zones, Trailblazers
- M Mascots — drive through them for credits
- PH Photo & landmark spots (Collection Journal stamps)
- H The Estate — your customisable property
- G Garages — 8 car-display + fast-travel points
- A Aftermarket Cars — green CT icons on the map
- T Treasure Cars — photo-clue only, no marker until found

## Barn Finds
**Count**: 15 (IGN, Windows Central, PC Gamer, Red Bull).
Barn Finds are classic cars abandoned in barns across Japan, gated behind your Discover Japan stamps. There are 15 of them, unlocked in batches of one to four as you climb the seven Discover Japan stamp tiers from Visitor to Master Explorer. Wikipedia does not enumerate this mechanic, so the roster below is guide-sourced and cross-checked between IGN, Windows Central, PC Gamer and Red Bull.

### All 15 Barn Finds

| # | Car | Unlocked at | Region | Where to look |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 2005 Honda NSX-R GT | Visitor (yellow, 1/7) | Ohtani | In the woods along the north-west edge of the search area, where the two nearby roads pincer together. Rough terrain — don't bring a slow city car. |
| 2 | 1969 Toyota 2000GT | Sightseer (green, 2/7) | Ito | North Ito, not far from Minka House. Small patch of trees near the seawall on the south-eastern edge of the search zone, between the two paths down to the beach. |
| 3 | 1987 Ford Sierra Cosworth RS500 | Sightseer (green, 2/7) | Ito | Southern Ito, up the small wooded hill just south of the crossroads junction on the southern edge of the search zone. You can almost see it from the road. |
| 4 | 1971 Nissan Skyline 2000GT-R | Traveller (blue, 3/7) | Nangan | Far south of the search area, past the houses on the main road — a dirt path leads off towards the barn. |
| 5 | 1989 Nissan Pao | Traveller (blue, 3/7) | Minamino | Woods on the north-east edge of the search area, down a dirt path leading off the main road. The Dodge Charger R/T Treasure Car is a short drive east. |
| 6 | 1982 Porsche 911 Turbo 3.3 | Pathfinder (pink, 4/7) | Ohtani / Tokyo City | Bamboo forest beside the dirt road between the two main roads that lead to Mei's House, in the Ohtani side of the search zone. |
| 7 | 1984 Peugeot 205 Turbo 16 | Pathfinder (pink, 4/7) | Shimanoyama | Barn at the end of the wide dirt road that climbs a short hill from the main road, in the north-east of the search zone. Visible from the main road. |
| 8 | 1962 Lincoln Continental | Pathfinder (pink, 4/7) | Hokubu | Patch of trees beside the colourful flower fields just south of the centre of the search zone, near Shikisai-No-Oka. |
| 9 | 1998 Nissan #23 Pennzoil NISMO Skyline GT-R | Pathfinder (pink, 4/7) | Takashiro | Woods on the eastern edge of the search area, inside the 'u' bend of the road. The Lancer Evolution III GSR Treasure Car is by the waterfall nearby. |
| 10 | 1997 Mitsubishi Montero Evolution | Navigator (orange, 5/7) | Shimanoyama | Forest on the south-west edge of the search area; a dirt path leads in from the main road not far from the Bandai Azuma Skyline Drift Zone. |
| 11 | 1997 Lamborghini Diablo SV | Navigator (orange, 5/7) | Ito | Eastern edge of the search zone — down the hill with the felled trees opposite the blue digger, then around the bend on your right. |
| 12 | 1998 Nissan R390 (GT1) | Adventurer (purple, 6/7) | Ohtani | Dirt path along the north-eastern edge of the search area, near the Ohtani / Shimanoyama border. Also reachable from the Bridge Underpasses Trailblazer start gate. |
| 13 | 2005 Mitsubishi #1 Sierra Sierra Enterprises Lancer Evolution Time Attack | Adventurer (purple, 6/7) | Shimanoyama | Woods almost dead centre of the search area, overlooking Narai-Juku to the south. Take the high dirt road up from the Narai-Juku Circuit road race, then the path on your right. |
| 14 | 1983 Nissan #11 Tomica Skyline Turbo Super Silhouette | Master Explorer (gold, 7/7) | Ito | South-western edge of the search area. Where the main road enters the zone from the west, a wide dirt path runs south between some oddly skinny trees — easy to pick out on the map. |
| 15 | 1991 Mazda #55 Mazda 787B | Master Explorer (gold, 7/7) | Takashiro | Woods directly north of the search area, past the buildings, walking trails and farmland. Dirt path off the main road at the north-west edge of the zone. |

**How to find them:**
- Earn Discover Japan stamps — mascots smashed, food delivery jobs, street and touge races, and above all the yellow-badge story missions.
- Each stamp tier unlocks new Barn Find rumours (generally one to four at a time).
- A purple circle appears on the map — drive into it to reveal the barn's rough area.
- Search the circle for the barn; you can spot it fast by flying a Drone over the zone.
- The car is sent for restoration, which takes real time — a couple of hours up to several days. You can pay credits to skip it, but it is rarely worth it.

_We deliberately give descriptive landmark pointers, not map coordinates — the four guides we cross-checked describe these spots in words, and inventing coordinate pairs would be exactly the kind of fabrication this site avoids. We track all 15 Barn Finds; some interactive maps still list only 14 (a stale count, corrected against IGN's May 2026 update). Restoration takes real time (hours to days), so start hunting early._

## Treasure Cars
**Count**: 9 (GamesRadar, PC Gamer, Gamereactor, GamingBolt).
Treasure Cars are abandoned vehicles hidden across Japan, found only via photo clues (no map marker until you are nearly on top of one). There are nine — one per region of the mainland, with the ninth in Tokyo City. Unlike Barn Finds they need no stamp progression and no restoration: just drive up and claim them, in any order. Wikipedia does not enumerate this mechanic, so the roster below is guide-sourced and cross-checked across four outlets.

### All 9 Treasure Cars

| # | Car | Region | Where to look |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1991 Nissan Figaro | Tokyo City | Small car park on the Tokyo Bay waterfront — north-east of the Rainbow Bridge, north-west of the Daikoku Parking Area marker. |
| 2 | 1969 Dodge Charger R/T | Minamino | Behind the clubhouse and convenience store buildings on the east side of the golf course, near the line of golf carts. The course sits centrally, close to the Airfield Trail dirt race. |
| 3 | 1985 Mazda RX-7 GSL-SE | Ohtani | By the radio towers on the western border where Ohtani meets Shimanoyama — not the towers further north. |
| 4 | 1987 Porsche 959 | Shimanoyama | Just outside the convenience store on the south-eastern side of Narai-Juku, the small town in the north of the region. |
| 5 | 1981 BMW M1 | Hokubu | Under the railway bridge surrounded by crop fields in the north of the region, roughly north-east of the Shikisai-No-Oka flower fields. Look for the support column covered in scaffolding. |
| 6 | 1995 Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution III GSR | Takashiro | On the dirt road in front of Nachi Falls in the north-western corner of the region. The waterfall also hides a 5,000 XP Bonus Board. |
| 7 | 1974 Lancia Stratos HF Stradale | Sotoyama | Beside a lone building on the mountain along the east–west main road that forms the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route. Head for the base of the tallest ski path. |
| 8 | 2005 Ford GT | Nangan | Beach car park at the end of an unmarked dirt track at the easternmost point of the region, off the coastal road that looks back towards Tokyo City. |
| 9 | 1985 Nissan Safari Turbo | Ito | At the base of one of the wind turbines along the Turbine Trail Drift Zone in the north of the region. |

**How to find them:**
- Drive around Japan; Mei hands you a photo clue when you pass near a Treasure Car.
- The photo is the puzzle — study the background (mountains, signs, road shape) to narrow it down.
- Find the exact spot, claim the car, and it's in your collection for free — no restoration wait.
- Once discovered, the location stays marked on your map.
- A systematic north-to-south sweep covers all nine in a couple of hours.

_All nine are free. GamingBolt reports that claiming every Treasure Car unlocks the 'Lost and Found' badge — treat that one as single-sourced. We show GamingBolt's map-grid label (letter+number, e.g. D 234) for each car as a navigation aid — that is their overlay grid, not an in-game GPS readout, and we still publish landmark descriptions rather than invented coordinates. Barn Finds remain landmark-only, since no trusted numeric source exists for them._

## Aftermarket Cars
Aftermarket Cars are secondhand vehicles scattered across the map. They match your current campaign progression, come fully tuned with kits, and cost less than the Autoshow. (Wikipedia confirms deep car customisation but does not define this specific system; details below are community-sourced.)

**How to get them:**
- Watch the minimap for green CT car icons while driving to events.
- Drive up and buy directly — no auction house needed.
- They're a cheap, ready-to-race alternative to the Autoshow early on.

## Forza Edition Cars
Forza Edition (FE) cars are rare, specially-tuned variants found on the road and as rewards. Wikipedia does not confirm this category; the examples below are community-sourced.
- **Lexus LFA FE** — Ultimate reward for Street Racing & Touge.
- **Subaru Vivio FE** — Horizon Life Events reward.
- **Nissan Nismo GT-R '24** — Top reward from Touge & Street Rivals.

## Festival Playlist

**Data as of August 31, 2026. Next season reset: September 3, 2026 (Spring season, final week of Series 4).** Reward cars change every Thursday. If today is past the date above, treat this page as out of date and check the official Forza channels before planning your week.

The Festival Playlist is the live content backbone of every Forza Horizon. A new season drops each Thursday across a four-week Series; each season hands out exclusive cars, credits and accolades. Track your own progress below — we never list rewards we can't verify.

| Winter | Aug 27 – Sep 3 | current | 1974 Toyota Celica GT | 1989 Toyota MR2 SC |
| Spring | Sep 3 – Sep 10 | upcoming | 1988 Mitsubishi Starion ESI-R | 1968 Dodge Dart HEMI Super Stock |

#### Series reward cars (bank points across the whole month)
- **1970 Honda N600** — 80 pts
- **1967 Renault 8 Gordini** — 160 pts

New to Horizon this series: 1970 Honda N600, 1974 Toyota Celica GT, 1988 Mitsubishi Starion ESI-R, 2018 Exomotive Exocet Sport V8 XP-5.

- **Aug 13** — 1987 Porsche #203 Porsche AG 961 (past)

- **Sep 3** — 1983 Nissan Skyline 2000 Turbo (upcoming)

Next up: Series 5 — British Automotive. Announced by Playground Games as the follow-up to Horizon Mascot Party; reward cars not yet published.


Standard event types each season (structure is stable across the series):
- **Forzathon Daily** — 7 small challenges, refresh daily Reward: Forzathon Points.
- **Weekly Forzathon** — One themed 4-part chain Reward: Car + Forzathon Points.
- **The Trial** — Co-op championship vs. Unbeatable AI Reward: Exclusive Car.
- **Seasonal Playground** — PvP playground games Reward: Exclusive Car.
- **Seasonal PR Stunts** — Danger Sign, Speed Trap, Speed Zone, Drift Zone & Jumps Reward: Super Wheelspins.
- **Seasonal Championships** — 2-3 themed races Reward: Exclusive Cars.
- **Treasure Hunt** — Solve the clue, find the chest Reward: Car + 100k Credits.
- **Photo Challenge** — #Hashtag snapshot at a location Reward: Car.
- **Horizon Arcade** — Co-op mini-game series Reward: Car.
- **Monthly Rivals** — Time attack vs. the world Reward: Credits.

_Season rewards reset weekly and are only claimable during their own week. Series rewards need a bigger point total across the whole month and are the more desirable cars. Seasons roll over every Thursday at 09:30 ET / 06:30 PT._

## Houses & property
Two different sets of "8" in Horizon Japan — and mixing them up is the single most common error in FH6 property guides. Wikipedia confirms one headline property, The Estate, plus 8 Garages that double as fast-travel and car-display points [WIKI]. Separately, community guides enumerate 8 buyable player houses, each with a permanent perk that stays active wherever you spawn; Wikipedia does not enumerate those, so they are labelled community-sourced [RPS, TECH, FH6GUIDE]. The Estate (Yashiki House) is the headline — a fully buildable plot you shape with an upgraded EventLab toolset. Houses unlock through the seven Discover Japan stamp tiers (yellow Visitor → green Sightseer → blue Traveller → pink Pathfinder → orange Navigator → purple Adventurer → gold Master Explorer).

### Mei's House
- **Region**: Ohtani
- **Price**: Free
- **Perk**: Wheeler Dealer — Unlocks car trading at the Autoshow
- **Unlocked at**: Yellow Stamp (tutorial)
- Auto-unlocks after the tutorial. Grab it first — it opens Autoshow car trading.

### The Estate (Yashiki House)
- **Region**: Hokubu
- **Price**: 10,000 Cr
- **Perk**: Estate Builder — Build & customise tracks, structures, water and foliage
- **Unlocked at**: 1st Discover Japan Stamp
- The buildable base. Clear the 19 objects blocking the land, pay 10,000 Cr, and you get a permanent, friends-visitable plot. Up to 12 players can co-create via Horizon Collab.

### Tokyo House
- **Region**: Tokyo City
- **Price**: 3,000,000 Cr (free with VIP)
- **Perk**: Daily Wheelspin — One free spin every day
- **Unlocked at**: Yellow Stamp
- Best long-term credit investment. VIP players get it for free.

### Minka House
- **Region**: Ito
- **Price**: 450,000 Cr
- **Perk**: Credit Stunts — +10% credits from Stunt Party
- **Unlocked at**: Green Stamp
- Solid mid-game earner from skill-chain stunts.

### Hakusan Mountain Lodge
- **Region**: Sotoyama
- **Price**: 635,000 Cr
- **Perk**: +1 Garage Slot & +10% Horizon Life credits — Extra display slot + bonus life credits
- **Unlocked at**: Blue Stamp
- Best ROI — the extra garage slot is a genuine bonus.

### Fuji Unkai House
- **Region**: Shimanoyama
- **Price**: 830,000 Cr
- **Perk**: Career Driver — +10% credits from Jobs
- **Unlocked at**: Orange Stamp
- Best for players who grind Jobs and careers.

### Soko 78
- **Region**: Tokyo City
- **Price**: 980,000 Cr
- **Perk**: Import/Export — -5% Autoshow discount
- **Unlocked at**: Purple Stamp
- Pays for itself after a few high-end car purchases.

### Vision House
- **Region**: Ohtani
- **Price**: 1,500,000 Cr
- **Perk**: +1 Garage Slot & +10% LINK Skill score — Extra slot + convoy skill bonus
- **Unlocked at**: Gold Stamp (Master Explorer)
- Endgame property for convoy players; needs serious time to unlock.

### Garages (8) — a different set of 8
Horizon Japan has 8 Garages — a different set of 8 from the buyable houses above. These double as free fast-travel points and shareable car-display spaces with customisable, community-downloadable interiors [WIKI]. The Estate is the only property Wikipedia confirms; the 8 Garages are the other Wikipedia-confirmed piece of the property picture.

Don't confuse these with houses — they're fast-travel/car-display points, not owned properties.

## Critical reception (Wikipedia)
Forza Horizon 6 received universal acclaim. On Metacritic it scored 90/100 (PC) and 91/100 (Xbox Series X/S); OpenCritic recorded a 100% recommend rate across 142 reviews [WIKI].
- IGN: 10/10
- Eurogamer: 5/5
- Giant Bomb: 5/5
- Video Games Chronicle: 5/5
- Game Informer: 9.25/10
- Destructoid: 9/10
- PCGamesN: 9/10
- Shacknews: 9/10
- Pure Xbox: 9/10
- Hardcore Gamer: 4.5/5
- TechRadar: 4.5/5
- GamesRadar+: 4/5
- GameSpot: 8/10
- PC Gamer (US): 84/100

Critics praised the Japan setting, the expansive open world, the driving feel, and the variety of activities. PC Gamer called the cutscene dialogue "bland" and GamesRadar+ called the story "shallow"; some noted the structure felt conservative [WIKI].

Steam user reviews (as of Aug 31, 2026): On Steam the all-platform user score sits at roughly 80% positive. The Simplified Chinese region is the clear outlier — about 67–69% (Mixed / 褒贬不一) across roughly 8,000–10,000 reviews, the lowest of any language — while the other regions average about 86% (Very Positive). The gap is driven by localisation-quality and Xbox-network complaints, not the Japan setting.

## Development & release (Wikipedia)
Forza Horizon 6 is developed by Playground Games with assistance from Turn 10 Studios, and published by Xbox Game Studios [WIKI].
- **Sep 25, 2025** — Revealed at Tokyo Game Show [WIKI].
- **Dec 2025** — Turn 10 Studios shifts to focus on Forza Horizon 6 [WIKI].
- **Jan 22, 2026** — Gameplay premieres at the Xbox Developer Direct [WIKI].
- **Apr 20, 2026** — Limited-edition Xbox controller and headset announced (launch May 19) [WIKI].
- **May 7–31, 2026** — Crunchyroll subscribers receive a free car voucher [WIKI].
- **May 10, 2026** — 155 GB preload leaked/decrypted on Steam; Playground banned the leaker [WIKI].
- **May 15, 2026** — Premium early access begins [WIKI].
- **May 19, 2026** — Worldwide launch on Windows and Xbox Series X/S [WIKI].
- **May 21, 2026** — Surpasses 6 million players [WIKI].
- **May 24, 2026** — 300,000 concurrent players on Steam — 52nd-highest all-time peak [WIKI].
- **Aug 27, 2026** — PS5 version reported delayed — Tom Warren (The Verge) says he does not expect it on PS5 in 2026; IGN reports the same from its own sources. Warren stressed it is "definitely still releasing" — delayed, not cancelled. Microsoft and Playground Games have not issued an official statement or a revised date [VERGE, IGN].
- **Late 2026** — PlayStation 5 version originally planned — superseded by the delay reports above. Status: delayed, date TBC.
